literal: Empress Lou of Shenwu
idiomatic: Empress Lou of Shenwu

literal: Empress Ming, Lady Lou, taboo name Zhaojun, was the daughter of Neigan, posthumously appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Empress Ming, née Lou, whose personal name was Zhaojun, was the daughter of Neigan, posthumously appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.

literal: From youth she was bright and perceptive; powerful clans sought her in marriage many times, yet she would not go.
idiomatic: From girlhood she was bright and perceptive. Powerful clans sought her hand again and again, yet she would not consent.

literal: When she saw Shenwu performing labor on the city wall, she was startled and said: "This is truly my husband.
idiomatic: When she saw Gao Huan laboring on the city wall, she started and said, "This is truly my husband.

literal: " She then sent a maid to convey her feelings, and repeatedly sent private funds so that he might betroth her; her parents, having no choice, consented.
idiomatic: " She sent a maid to convey her feelings and repeatedly sent private funds so that he might betroth her; her parents, having no choice, consented.

literal: Once Shenwu had the will to restore order, he spent his estate to win over heroes; in secret plots and hidden stratagems the empress always took part.
idiomatic: Once Gao Huan resolved to restore order, he spent his estate to win over heroes; in secret plots and hidden stratagems Empress Lou always took part.

literal: When he was enfeoffed Princess Consort of Bohai, all affairs of the inner quarters were decided by her.
idiomatic: When he was enfeoffed Princess Consort of Bohai, all affairs of the inner quarters were decided by her.

literal: The empress was lofty, clear, and stern in judgment; she always observed thrift; when going out to external residences, her attendants never exceeded ten.
idiomatic: The empress was lofty in judgment, clear-minded, and stern; she always observed thrift, and when she went out to external residences her attendants never exceeded ten.

literal: Her nature was generous and she was not jealous; Shenwu's concubines and attendants she all treated with favor.
idiomatic: Her nature was generous and free of jealousy; Gao Huan's concubines and attendants she treated with equal favor.

literal: Once when Shenwu was about to march west on campaign, the empress at night bore twins, a boy and a girl; those beside her, finding the situation perilous, asked to send word after Shenwu.
idiomatic: Once, as Gao Huan was about to march west on campaign, the empress gave birth at night to twins, a boy and a girl. Those beside her, finding the situation perilous, asked to send word after him.

literal: The empress would not listen and said: "The king has gone forth to command a great army — how can he lightly leave the command tent on my account.
idiomatic: The empress would not hear of it. "The king has gone forth to command a great army," she said. "How can he lightly leave the command tent on my account?

literal: Life and death are fate — what use is it if he comes back!
idiomatic: Life and death are fate — what use is it if he comes back!

literal: " When Shenwu heard of it, he sighed in admiration for a long while.
idiomatic: " When Gao Huan heard of it, he sighed in admiration for a long while.

literal: After the defeat at Shaya, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand picked cavalry, saying he could certainly recover it.
idiomatic: After the defeat at Shaya, Hou Jing repeatedly asked for twenty thousand picked cavalry, saying he could certainly recover the lost ground.

literal: Shenwu was pleased and told the empress.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was pleased and told the empress.

literal: The empress said: "If it comes about as he says, could there be any coming back — gain the otter, lose Jing; what profit is there.
idiomatic: The empress said, "If things go as he promises, do you suppose he would ever return? You would gain some paltry conquest and lose Hou Jing — what profit is there in that?

literal: " Thereupon he desisted.
idiomatic: " Thereupon he desisted.

literal: Shenwu, pressed by the Rouran, wished to marry their princess but had not yet decided.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, pressed by the Rouran, wished to marry their princess but had not yet decided.

literal: The empress said: "This is a great plan for the state — do not hesitate.
idiomatic: The empress said, "This is a great plan for the state — do not hesitate.

literal: " When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress vacated the main chamber to lodge her.
idiomatic: " When the Rouran princess arrived, the empress vacated the main chamber to lodge her.

literal: Shenwu, ashamed, bowed and apologized to her, saying: "She will notice — please sever all ties and do not look back.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, ashamed, bowed and apologized to her, saying, "She will notice — please sever all ties and do not look back.

literal: " She loved all the sons as if they were her own; she personally spun and wove, giving each man one robe and one pair of trousers.
idiomatic: " She loved all the sons as if they were her own; she personally spun and wove, giving each man one robe and one pair of trousers.

literal: With her own hands she sewed military garments to lead those beside her.
idiomatic: With her own hands she sewed military garments to set an example for those beside her.

literal: Her younger brother Zhao attained distinction through merit; as for the rest of her kin, she never once asked for noble rank on their behalf.
idiomatic: Her younger brother Zhao attained distinction through merit; as for the rest of her kin, she never once asked for noble rank on their behalf.

literal: She always said that talent should be employed when found, and that righteousness must not let private feeling disorder public duty.
idiomatic: She always said that talent should be employed when found, and that righteousness must not let private feeling disorder public duty.

literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to the throne, she was advanced to Grand Consort.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded to the throne, she was advanced to Grand Consort.

literal: When Wenxuan was about to receive the Wei abdication, the empress firmly refused to permit it, and the emperor therefore desisted.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang was about to receive the Wei abdication, the empress firmly refused to permit it, and the emperor therefore desisted.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Xuanxun.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Xuanxun.

literal: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: When the Emperor of Jinan succeeded, she was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

literal: Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing Yang Yin and others received the testamentary edict to assist in government and kept the princes at a distance in suspicion.
idiomatic: Chief Minister Yang Yin and others received the testamentary edict to assist in government and kept the princes at a distance in suspicion.

literal: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Xiaozhao and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing and enthroning.
idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager secretly joined Gao Yan and the great generals in fixing a plan to execute them, and issued an edict deposing one ruler and enthroning another.

literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan succeeded, she again became Empress Dowager.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, the empress dowager again issued an edict enthroning Emperor Wucheng.

literal: In the spring of the second year of Daning, the empress dowager fell ill; her garments suddenly lifted of themselves, and following a sorceress's words she changed her surname to Shi.
idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Daning, the empress dowager fell ill; her garments suddenly lifted of themselves, and following a sorceress's words she changed her surname to Shi.

literal: On the xinchou day of the fourth month she died at the Northern Palace, aged sixty-two.
idiomatic: On the xinchou day of the fourth month she died at the Northern Palace, aged sixty-two.

literal: On the jiashen day of the fifth month she was interred with Shenwu at Yiping Tomb.
idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the fifth month she was interred with Gao Huan at Yiping Tomb.

literal: The empress dowager in all bore six sons and two daughters, each pregnancy attended by a dream: when she conceived Wenxiang she dreamed of a severed dragon;
idiomatic: The empress dowager in all bore six sons and two daughters, each pregnancy attended by a dream: when she conceived Gao Cheng she dreamed of a severed dragon;

literal: when she conceived Wenxuan she dreamed of a great dragon whose head and tail joined heaven and earth, mouth open and eyes moving, its aspect terrifying;
idiomatic: when she conceived Gao Yang she dreamed of a great dragon whose head and tail joined heaven and earth, mouth open and eyes moving, its aspect terrifying;

literal: when she conceived Xiaozhao she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;
idiomatic: when she conceived Gao Yan she dreamed of a writhing dragon upon the ground;

literal: when she conceived Wucheng she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;
idiomatic: when she conceived Gao Zhan she dreamed of a dragon bathing in the sea;

literal: when she conceived the two Wei empresses she both dreamed of the moon entering the bosom;
idiomatic: when she conceived the two Wei empresses she both dreamed of the moon entering the bosom;

literal: when she conceived the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling she dreamed of rats entering beneath the garments.
idiomatic: when she conceived the Princes of Xiangcheng and Boling she dreamed of rats entering beneath the garments.

literal: Before the empress dowager died, a children's rhyme said: "Nine dragons — when the mother dies, no mourning."
idiomatic: Before the empress dowager died, a children's rhyme ran: "Nine dragons — when the mother dies, no mourning."

literal: When the empress dowager died, Wucheng did not change his garments and kept his crimson robe as before.
idiomatic: When the empress dowager died, Wucheng did not change his garments and kept his crimson robe as before.

literal: Before long he ascended the Three Towers, set out wine, and made music.
idiomatic: Before long he ascended the Three Towers, set out wine, and made music.

literal: The emperor's daughter brought a white robe; the emperor was angry and cast it down from the tower.
idiomatic: The emperor's daughter brought a white robe; the emperor was angry and cast it down from the tower.

literal: He Shikai asked that the music be stopped; the emperor was greatly angered and beat him.
idiomatic: He Shikai asked that the music be stopped; the emperor was greatly angered and beat him.

literal: The emperor among his brothers by birth was actually ninth — surely this was the omen's fulfillment.
idiomatic: The emperor among his brothers by birth was actually ninth — surely this was the omen's fulfillment.

literal: Empress Yuan of Wenxiang
idiomatic: Empress Yuan of Wenxiang

literal: Reverent Empress Yuan of Wenxiang was the elder sister of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.
idiomatic: Reverent Empress Yuan of Wenxiang was the elder sister of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.

literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and given in marriage to Wenxiang.
idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei she was enfeoffed Princess of Fengyi and given in marriage to Gao Cheng.

literal: Her bearing and virtue were both beautiful; in harmony and reverence she exhausted every measure.
idiomatic: Her bearing and virtue were both beautiful; in harmony and reverence she exhausted every measure.

literal: When she first bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, Wenxiang was then heir; on the third day Emperor Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and bestowed brocades, silks, and cloth in ten thousand bolts.
idiomatic: When she first bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian, Gao Cheng was then heir; on the third day Emperor Xiaojing visited the heir's residence and bestowed brocades, silks, and cloth in ten thousand bolts.

literal: The heir declined and asked instead to receive the gifts and presents of the nobles; thereupon ten rooms were filled.
idiomatic: The heir declined and asked instead to receive the gifts and presents of the nobles; thereupon ten rooms were filled.

literal: Next she bore two princesses.
idiomatic: Next she bore two princesses.

literal: When Wenxuan received the abdication, she was honored as Empress of Wenxiang and dwelt in Jingde Palace.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang received the abdication, she was honored as Empress of Wenxiang and dwelt in Jingde Palace.

literal: By the sixth year of Tianbao, Wenxuan gradually fell into madness; he then moved her to a residence at Gaoyang and took her storehouses, saying: "My elder brother once violated my wife — now I must repay him.
idiomatic: By the sixth year of Tianbao, Gao Yang gradually fell into madness; he then moved her to a residence at Gaoyang and seized her storehouses, saying, "My elder brother once violated my wife — now I must repay him.

literal: " Thereupon he violated the empress.
idiomatic: " Thereupon he violated the empress.

literal: Every woman of the Gao clan, close or distant in kinship, he had those beside him violate in turn before her.
idiomatic: Every woman of the Gao clan, close or distant in kinship, he had those beside him violate in turn before her.

literal: He made a rope of hemp and had Princess Andrade of Wei mount it, with men pushing and pulling her; he also ordered barbarians to humiliate her cruelly.
idiomatic: He made a rope of hemp and had Princess Andrade of Wei mount it, with men pushing and pulling her; he also ordered barbarians to humiliate her cruelly.

literal: The emperor also exposed himself and showed himself to the assembled officials.
idiomatic: The emperor also exposed himself and displayed his nakedness before the assembled officials.

literal: In the Wuping era the empress died and was given joint burial at Yiping Tomb.
idiomatic: In the Wuping era the empress died and was given joint burial at Yiping Tomb.

literal: Empress Li of Wenxuan
idiomatic: Empress Li of Wenxuan

literal: Empress Li of Wenxuan, taboo name Zu'e, was the daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao Commandery.
idiomatic: Empress Li of Wenxuan, whose personal name was Zu'e, was the daughter of Li Xizong of Zhao Commandery.

literal: Her bearing and virtue were exceedingly beautiful.
idiomatic: Her bearing and virtue were exceedingly beautiful.

literal: At first she was Lady of the Duke of Taiyuan.
idiomatic: At first she was Lady of the Duke of Taiyuan.

literal: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said a Han woman could not be mother to the realm and that a more beautiful match should be chosen.
idiomatic: When the emperor was about to establish the central palace, Gao Longzhi and Gao Dezheng said a Han woman could not be mother to the realm and that a more beautiful match should be chosen.

literal: Yang Yin firmly requested following the Han and Wei precedents and not changing the original consort.
idiomatic: Yang Yin firmly requested following the Han and Wei precedents and not changing the original consort.

literal: Yet Dezheng still firmly asked to depose the empress and install Lady Duan as Honored Consort, wishing thereby to win the support of meritorious nobles; the emperor in the end did not follow him and established the empress.
idiomatic: Yet Dezheng still firmly asked to depose the empress and install Lady Duan as Honored Consort, wishing thereby to win the support of meritorious nobles; the emperor in the end did not follow him and established the empress.

literal: The emperor loved to beat and flog the palace women, even to the point of killing some; only toward Empress Li did he show ritual respect.
idiomatic: The emperor loved to beat and flog the palace women, even to the point of killing some; only toward Empress Li did he show ritual respect.

literal: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was renamed Khedun Empress.
idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tianbao she was renamed Khedun Empress.

literal: When Xiaozhao succeeded, she was reduced to Zhaoxin Palace and styled Empress of Zhaoxin.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan succeeded, she was reduced to Zhaoxin Palace and styled Empress of Zhaoxin.

literal: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into illicit relations, saying: "If you do not consent, I shall kill your son.
idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne, he forced the empress into illicit relations, saying, "If you do not consent, I shall kill your son.

literal: " The empress, in fear, complied.
idiomatic: " The empress, in fear, complied.

literal: Later she became pregnant; Prince Shao of Taiyuan came to her gate but could not see her, and angrily said: "Does the boy not know? My elder sister's belly is great — that is why she will not see the boy.
idiomatic: Later she became pregnant; Prince Shao of Taiyuan came to her gate but could not see her, and angrily said, "Does the boy not know? My elder sister's belly is great — that is why she will not see the boy.

literal: " When the empress heard it, she was deeply ashamed; from this she bore daughters and did not rear them.
idiomatic: " When the empress heard it, she was deeply ashamed; from this she bore daughters and did not rear them.

literal: The emperor drew his blade and cursed, saying: "You killed my daughter — why should I not kill your son!
idiomatic: The emperor drew his blade and cursed, saying, "You killed my daughter — why should I not kill your son!

literal: " Before the empress he beat Shao to death.
idiomatic: " Before the empress he beat Shao to death.

literal: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier still, stripped her naked, and beat her at random; she cried to heaven without cease.
idiomatic: The empress wept greatly; the emperor grew angrier still, stripped her naked, and beat her at random; she cried to heaven without cease.

literal: She was placed in a silk sack; blood dripped and soaked through; she was cast into the canal water; only after a long while did she revive, and an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.
idiomatic: She was placed in a silk sack; blood dripped and soaked through; she was cast into the canal water; only after a long while did she revive, and an ox-cart carried her to Miaosheng Nunnery.

literal: The empress by nature loved the Buddhist Law; on this account she became a nun.
idiomatic: The empress by nature loved the Buddhist Law; on this account she became a nun.

literal: When Qi fell she entered the Pass.
idiomatic: When Qi fell she entered the Pass.

literal: In the Sui era she was able to return to Zhao Commandery.
idiomatic: In the Sui era she was able to return to Zhao Commandery.

literal: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao
idiomatic: Empress Yuan of Xiaozhao

literal: Empress Hu of Wucheng
idiomatic: Empress Hu of Wucheng

literal: Empress Hu of Wucheng was the daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.
idiomatic: Empress Hu of Wucheng was the daughter of Hu Yan of Anding.

literal: Her mother was a daughter of Lu Daoyue of Fanyang; when she first conceived, a barbarian monk came to the gate and said: "In this house's gourd-reeds there is a moon"; thereupon the empress was born.
idiomatic: Her mother was a daughter of Lu Daoyue of Fanyang; when she first conceived, a barbarian monk came to the gate and said, "In this house's gourd-reeds there is a moon"; thereupon the empress was born.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao she was selected as Princess Consort of Changguang.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era she was selected as Princess Consort of Changguang.

literal: On the day she bore the Last Emperor, a bird cried above the birthing pavilion.
idiomatic: On the day she bore the Last Emperor, a bird cried above the birthing pavilion.

literal: When Wucheng died she was honored as Empress Dowager; Nurse Lu and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as governors.
idiomatic: When Wucheng died she was honored as Empress Dowager; Nurse Lu and He Shikai secretly plotted to kill Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery and sent out Lou Dingyuan and Gao Wenyao as governors.

literal: He and Lu fawned upon the empress dowager to every extreme.
idiomatic: He and Lu fawned upon the empress dowager to every extreme.

literal: In Wucheng's time the empress had been familiar with the eunuchs.
idiomatic: In Wucheng's time the empress had been familiar with the eunuchs.

literal: Wucheng favored He Shikai; he often played polo with the empress, and through this came to commit adultery with her.
idiomatic: Wucheng favored He Shikai; he often played polo with the empress, and through this came to commit adultery with her.

literal: After Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples, and again had relations with the monk Tanxian.
idiomatic: After Wucheng's death she often went out to Buddhist temples, and again had relations with the monk Tanxian.

literal: She spread gold coins beneath Tanxian's mat and hung upon the wall of Tanxian's room a precious decorated barbarian couch that Wucheng had used in life.
idiomatic: She spread gold coins beneath Tanxian's mat and hung upon the wall of Tanxian's room a precious decorated barbarian couch that Wucheng had used in life.

literal: She then placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, using the pretext of listening to lectures, and day and night shared Tanxian's bed.
idiomatic: She then placed a hundred monks in the inner hall, using the pretext of listening to lectures, and day and night shared Tanxian's bed.

literal: She made Tanxian Director of Buddhist Affairs.
idiomatic: She made Tanxian Director of Buddhist Affairs.

literal: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager while jesting with Tanxian, even calling her the Grand Sovereign.
idiomatic: Monks from afar pointed at the empress dowager while jesting with Tanxian, even calling her the Grand Sovereign.

literal: The emperor heard that the empress dowager was unrestrained but did not yet believe it; later, attending upon the empress dowager at court, he saw two young nuns, was pleased and summoned them — they were men; thereupon Tanxian's affair also came to light; all were executed by law, and the three Ladies of Yuan, Shan, and Wang were also killed — all were favorites of the empress dowager.
idiomatic: The emperor heard that the empress dowager was unrestrained but did not yet believe it; later, attending upon the empress dowager at court, he saw two young nuns, was pleased and summoned them — they were men; thereupon Tanxian's affair also came to light; all were executed by law, and the three Ladies of Yuan, Shan, and Wang were also killed — all were favorites of the empress dowager.

literal: The emperor himself escorted the empress dowager from Jinyang back to Ye; at Zimo they suddenly encountered a great wind.
idiomatic: The emperor himself escorted the empress dowager from Jinyang back to Ye; at Zimo they suddenly encountered a great wind.
